Considered the year's finale, this is one of the few festivals featuring fireworks in winter. Massive, lantern-lit floats are pulled up a steep hill against a backdrop of winter fireworks, creating a multi-layered spectacle of light.

### Gishi Matsuri

December 14, 2026 | Kyoto & Tokyo [...] Held in the Kayabuki no Sato thatched village of Nantan City, Kyoto, this event features the magical illumination of traditional thatched-roof houses, hundreds of snow lanterns, and LED lights from 5-7 PM. Special events on Jan 21, 2027, include traditional dance performances and mochi pounding. Shuttle bus from Kyoto and Osaka provided.

### Wakakusa Yamayaki

4th Saturday of January, 2027 | Nara [...] ### Toka Ebisu

January 8 – 12, 2027 | Kyoto

Kyoto’s first festival of the year is held at the Ebisu-jinja Shrine during which attendees pray to Ebisu, the god of commerce, for prosperity and good fortune in the new year. The god Ebisu is said to be hard of hearing and as a result the festival is a loud and boisterous one.

### Hatsu Basho

## Imperial Procession Reenactment in Kyoto / DEC

The city of Kyoto will hold a variety of events to celebrate the 400th anniversary of Emperor Go-Mizunoo’s visit to Nijo Castle, considered one of the largest events of the Edo period. The highlight will be an imperial procession reenactment on December 6th, featuring thousands of people and traditional music performances.
